candidate_topics: Control-History Utility Mapping (CHUM) for Industrial Time-Series Anomaly Detection
confirmed_findings: TEP G3 completed 340 tasks and passed the locked architecture-consensus gate: primary faults 4, 19, and 25 retained channel-level conditional utility in both TCN and Transformer.
Integrated Gradients selected the same top channel as CHUM in 7 of 8 primary architecture-fault cells, while agreement was materially weaker in negative or exploratory faults.
Corrected HAI 21.03 v2 external validation showed F1 above both F0 and capacity-matched F0-C in AUROC, AUPRC, and eTaF1 for all three seeds at comparable false-positive rates.

HAI conditional CHUM passed its preregistered external channel gate: 12 of 28 active controls passed imputer quality, and 5 directly targeted event-channel cells were stable with zero conditional FPR exceptions.
The first HAI run is invalidated and quarantined because training and test feature orders differed; no final claim uses it.
open_hypotheses: Control-history utility will remain stable under additional TEP seeds and imputer block-length or draw-count sensitivity checks.
Event-specific control-history utility will transfer to an external dataset where control channels are not directly attacked.
required_experiments: Human and supervisor approval of the final thesis title, research question, and claim wording
Manuscript synthesis from the validated G3, IG, HAI v2, and HAI conditional evidence package
Optional extra TEP seed and imputer block-length or draw-count sensitivity
Optional external validation without directly attacked control targets
recommended_gate: Evidence package complete; await explicit human approval before locking the final title and thesis claim, then begin manuscript drafting
